jaspers.text: 理性如同向所有人敞开的秘密，是每个人借由独立思考皆可步入的宁静空间。
jaspers.source: 引自《危机时代的哲学》，1959 年
jaspers.original: Reason is like an open secret that can become known to anyone at any time; it is the quiet space into which everyone can enter through his own thought.

damasio.text: 当你产生情绪时，大脑调动的正是漫长进化史中用来维系生命稳态的古老机制。
damasio.source: 加泰罗尼亚开放大学演讲，2005 年
damasio.original: When you have an emotion you are recruiting a variety of mechanisms that came in the long history of evolution, long before emotions arose, and those mechanisms all had to do with how an organism manages its life.

frankl.text: 意义疗法的任务是帮助他人看见生命的意义，但我们无法替别人“赋予”意义。
frankl.original: Specifically I see Logotherapy in helping others to see meaning in life. But we cannot 'give' meaning to the life of others.

levi-montalcini.text: 人生不应向平庸屈服，而应走出习惯与被动顺从的灰色地带。
levi-montalcini.source: 英文维基语录收录公开访谈
levi-montalcini.original: In life one should never give in, surrender oneself to mediocrity, but rather move out of that grey area where everything is habit and passive resignation.

cajal.text: 每个人，只要愿意，都能成为自己大脑的雕塑家。
cajal.source: 《给青年研究者的忠告》，1897 年
cajal.original: Any man could, if he were so inclined, be the sculptor of his own brain.

freud.text: 梦的解析，是通向心灵中潜意识活动知识的康庄大道。
freud.original: The interpretation of dreams is the royal road to a knowledge of the unconscious activities of the mind.

sacks.text: 生命形态的无穷多样性与奇妙之处，始终比世间一切事物更令我心潮澎湃。
sacks.source: 致古尔德书信，1995 年引录
sacks.original: The sense of diversity—of the wonder of innumerable forms of life—has always thrilled me beyond anything else.

friston.text: 低熵状态并非更接近死亡；消散与弥散构成的高熵，才是生命存在的终极边界。
friston.original: Low entropy states are not closer to death. Death is characterized by dissipation, decay and dispersion. It is the ultimate high entropy state—literally, the edge of our existential world.

beck.text: 认知疗法通过修正错误的观念与自我信号来缓解心理困扰，降低过度反应。
beck.source: 《认知疗法与情绪障碍》，1976 年
beck.original: Cognitive therapy seeks to alleviate psychological stresses by correcting faulty conceptions and self-signals. By correcting erroneous beliefs we can lower excessive reactions.

wundt.text: 从观察的立场来看，心理生命的开端极可能与一般生命的起源同样久远。
wundt.source: 《生理心理学原理》，1904 年英译本
wundt.original: From the standpoint of observation, then, we must regard it as a highly probable hypothesis that the beginnings of the mental life date from as far back as the beginnings of life at large.

sperry.text: 我从未认同仅凭纯客观术语、完全忽略主观体验就能完整解释大脑功能的观点。
sperry.source: 英文维基语录收录意识研究论述
sperry.original: I have never been entirely satisfied with the materialistic or behavioristic thesis that a complete explanation of brain function is possible in purely objective terms with no reference whatever to subjective experience.

helmholtz.text: 感觉神经传来的信号只是指向外部客体的符号，需要长期练习才能读懂其含义。
helmholtz.original: The sensations of our nerves of sense are mere symbols indicating certain external objects, and it is usually only after considerable practice that we acquire the power of drawing correct conclusions from our sensations.

pavlov.text: 事实是科学家的空气；没有事实，你永远无法飞翔，所谓理论也只是徒劳。
pavlov.source: 《致祖国科学青年的遗言》，《科学》，1936 年
pavlov.original: Facts are the air of a scientist. Without them you never can fly. Without them your 'theories' are vain efforts.

kandel.text: 神经生物学终将直面一个更为根本的课题：人类心理过程的生物学基础。
kandel.source: 《精神病学、精神分析与心智的新生物学》，2008 年
kandel.original: In the near future, neurobiology will address a matter of more general and fundamental importance: the biology of human mental processes.

huxley-andrew.text: 我非常清醒地意识到，我们为何拥有意识，至今仍没有科学解释。
huxley-andrew.source: 《经济学人》，2012 年 6 月 16 日
huxley-andrew.original: I am very conscious that there is no scientific explanation for the fact that we are conscious.

sherrington.text: 大脑过去是、将来也依然是个谜；日益丰硕的事实仍未交出心智如何诞生的钥匙。
sherrington.original: The brain is a mystery—it has been—and still will be. ... they all fail to give us a key to the mystery of how it creates—if it does create—our thoughts and feelings; that is, our mind.

gazzaniga.text: 我们逐渐明白，左半球会替右半球支配的举动编造出一套看似合情合理的故事。
gazzaniga.source: 《纽约科学院年鉴》访谈，2011 年
gazzaniga.original: We began to understand that the left hemisphere 'made up' a story as to why the patient did what he/she did.
